task_text: Cabinet Pick and Place: A tall wooden cabinet stands ahead of the hovering aerial manipulator, and a small soda can stands inside one of its shelf compartments, behind a closed sliding door. Get the can onto the top of the cabinet: AM-Bench counts success when the can's centre is less than 5 cm above a fixed height just below the cabinet's top surface (there is no horizontal condition) while the can moves slower than 0.1 m/s. Success: Success at a control step when both hold: (1) the can's root position (its body origin, the can's centre) satisfies 0 <= z - 1.67 < 0.05 m (drawer_top_z = 1.67 m above the environment origin, which is the world origin; i.e. 1.67 <= z < 1.72 m); (2) the norm of the can's linear velocity is < 0.1 m/s (can_place_velocity_threshold). Nothing else is tested: no horizontal (x, y) condition, no orientation, the can need not be released, and the door's position does not matter. AM-Bench also reports subtask criteria pulling_door_opened (|pull_door_slide - 0| >= 0.2 m), can_lifted (can z > its z at reset + 0.05 m) and can_placed_on_drawer (the success itself); they are informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 60 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 7200 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 7199th step.
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where AM-Bench's success check holds, when the task's episode length of 60 s of simulated time runs out (AM-Bench's time-out, at control step 7199), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
